title: Open-source multi-agent SDLC harness beats cold Claude Code by 7-75%
summary: AutoDev Studio, an open-source multi-agent software development lifecycle \(SDLC\) harness, reduces AI coding costs by 7-75% compared to a cold run of Claude Code on large repositories by building a persistent knowledge base via static analysis and local embedding indexing. This addresses a key inefficiency where AI coding agents re-explore repositories from scratch on every task, making localization costly. By caching repository knowledge, AutoDev Studio significantly lowers costs and improves scalability for AI-assisted software development on large codebases. The system uses a multi-agent pipeline including a PM agent, Dev agent, QA agent, and a reviewer from a different model family, with a bounded revise loop. It is provider agnostic and can run completely free offline using Groq&\#x27;s free tier and local embeddings, but loses on tiny edits or complex cross-cutting bugs where overhead or narrower fixes occur.
context: Typical AI coding agents, such as Claude Code, re-index and explore the repository for each new task to locate where changes should be made. AutoDev Studio pre-ingests the repository using static analysis and an embedding index, storing the knowledge persistently so that future tasks can look up relevant context instantly without repeated cold searches.
